description: Team Seg Faul consists of CENG students from Gebze Technical University who will participate in the hackathon by the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challange. We are planning to bring out a project that will be able to solve real-world problems using data analysis, sensor fusion and an interactive interface development.
summary: In Project ALAZ we focused on Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. Our aim was to prevent the inconveniencies caused by the dissimilarity of datasets provided by different satellites. For this purpose, we developed a website solution where a user can get access to a variety of functionalities such as visual representations of the fires on real world map, informative tables and graphics and fire calendars enabling them to obtain detailed information about the activities. We also developed codes to analyze and combine the datasets we obtained from official NASA archives, which allowed us to harmonize the data from both satellite sources and create solutions for representing the hotspot and fire activities at higher resolutions. We find our work quite useful and important for people from any level as it provides convenience for research and prevention of fire activities that will better the living conditions of the nature and the humankind.
details: As Seg Fault team we developed a website solution within the scope of Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. We believe this project is going to be really useful in detecting, analyzing and estimating fire activities. To outline the stages of the project development, we firstly decided to come up with a prototype of the interactive and informative website that will be restrained to activities that occurred within borders of Türkiye as it would be difficult and time consuming to analyze the data and develop the website for the whole earth in this limited time. In this context, we obtained real activity data for the both MODIS and VIIRS satellites from official NASA archives. For data analysis we used Python language because of its capability in big-data, in this stage we focused on eliminating low quality and recurring data and merging the data from the two sources. We also needed to combine data from close positions and dates in order to decrease the amount of activity caused by the satellite counting the same fire at every turn. At the stage of project development, we used GitHub and VSCode environments as they are very practical in corporation and management, we used the shared repository to update the project segments separately. For the web side we used HTML language and Javascript inline codes to manage the interactive windows and all the functionality. Also, we benefited from Google Gemini models as they are helpful in brainstorming, refining mathematical approaches and code development. We are confident that our project result meets the requirements of the challenge and provides users a fully interactive, modern-looking and informative website solution with all its functionalities.
